For odd m, n=m+1 and nodes x_j=3/8+j/(4m), mix a uniform background, a uniform even-node background and parity-conditioned Bin(m,1/2) weights to form nu_+/-; put mu_+/-=delta_0/4+3nu_+/-/4. The nominal pair has the same complete spectrum, ground gap 3/8, known ground weight 1/4, every excited weight >=3/(16n), and moments through m-1 equal. At t_m=4pi m, the source gives p_+=97/256, p_-=25/256, while Delta G=(3/4)exp(-3s/8)[(1-exp(-s/(4m)))/2]^m. G>=1/4 also controls logarithmic differences. Adaptive Gaussian relative entropy is <=N D^2/2, yielding N>=4/81[max{2,8m/B}]^(2m). Known spectrum, partition functions and the stated exact low moments do not distinguish this pair.

Inverse spectral Jacobi realization gives nearest-neighbour bulk chains with negative off-diagonals plus a known isolated reference, prepared as (1/2)e_ref+(sqrt(3)/2)e_0. The source derives |b|>=Delta sqrt(alpha)/3, hence bulk couplings >=1/(24m sqrt(m+1)). Excited-state spacings shrink as 1/m; only the ground gap is constant. Perturbations with norm <=1/(64t_m), common previously matched near-boundary coefficients and unchanged reference retain the exponential order and return-probability gap >=7/32. This is structured inverse-polynomial robustness. The nominal free common complete spectrum and spectral-weight floor are not asserted simultaneously for arbitrary perturbed pairs, and no unrestricted fixed-strength disorder result follows.

The upper construction uses M=ceil max{16T,log2(4/eps)}, a=min{B/M,1/16} and a truncated generalized-binomial polynomial in 1-exp(-ax). Expansion into G(la) values, 0<=l<=M, has l1 amplification <=S=2[2e(2+T/B)]^M and error <=2^-M+S delta. The reported sample cost is O((M+1)S^2 eps^-2 log((M+1)/zeta)); arithmetic and precision-bit costs are polynomial in the stated parameters, including log S. Statistical acquisition is exponential. Systematic bias, time-setting accuracy, preparation and decorrelation are charged separately; polynomially many precision bits can mean extremely fine absolute instrument tolerances. Fixed B gives a worst-case recoverable horizon Theta(log N/log log N); unlimited B gives Theta(log N). Individual spectra need not be hard.
